raw_case_text:
A 28-year-old male patient with a previous history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP), diagnosed six years ago but had stopped had treatment approximately five years ago, was hospitalized with clinical and epidemiological diagnosis of arbovirus infection (fever, asthenia, myalgia and arthralgia). On admission, thrombocytopenia (12,000/mm3) and anemia (8.0 g/dL) were observed (Table 1). Oral corticosteroid therapy was started with prednisone 1 mg/kg/day. On the third day of hospitalization, he had headache with vomiting, associated with mental confusion and, subsequently, motor aphasia and right hemiplegia. Considering the sudden worsening of the patient's overall conditions, he was referred to the intensive care unit. Nuclear magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed to rule out acute ischemic or hemorrhagic events. The neuroimaging examination showed no alterations. Faced with an acute neurological worsening, the possibility of TTP was considered. Analysis of the peripheral smear showed innumerable schizocytes, confirming the presence of TMA. Plasmapheresis and pulse therapy with methylprednisolone were started due to the hypothesis of TTP.
Serological results were IgM positive for chikungunya and dengue viruses, and initially, the presence of IgG only raised to chikungunya virus (Euroimmun Medizinische Labordiagnostika, Lubeck, Germany). Serological tests for hepatitis virus B and C were negative, as well as for retroviruses (only HIV). Regarding retroviruses, other representatives are not routinely investigated and, in this case, they were not suspected. The patient also had negative results for antinuclear antibody (ANA) (Table 2). During the follow-up, serological results for dengue and chikungunya were confirmed, at this time showing the presence of IgG antibodies to chikungunya as well as to dengue virus. The serological test for zika virus was not performed following guidelines from Brazilian Ministry of Health, which recommend not to test zika virus when serological tests for dengue and chikungunya are positive.
There was a decrease in lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (Table 1). Plasmapheresis was maintained until platelet counts remained higher than 150,000 for three consecutive days (Figure 1). Complete remission of neurological signs occurred after the first plasmapheresis.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 28-year-old male with a history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura presenting with acute fever, asthenia, myalgia, arthralgia, severe thrombocytopenia, and anemia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 28-year-old male with a history of immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) diagnosed 6 years prior presented with acute fever, asthenia, myalgia, and arthralgia. On hospital day 3, while receiving oral prednisone (1 mg/kg/day), he developed acute headache, vomiting, mental confusion, and rapidly progressed to motor aphasia and right hemiplegia. Emergent peripheral smear revealed abundant schistocytes, prompting ICU transfer for suspected thrombotic microangiopathy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) diagnosed 6 years prior, discontinued treatment approximately 5 years prior.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, asthenia, myalgia, arthralgia, headache, vomiting, confusion, aphasia, and right hemiplegia. Home medications: none prior to admission. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Neurological examination on hospital day 3: Mental confusion, expressive motor aphasia, and right-sided hemiplegia. Following the first session of plasmapheresis, neurological signs exhibited complete remission.
objective.routine_investigations: On admission: Platelet count 12,000/mm3, hemoglobin 8.0 g/dL. Peripheral blood smear: Innumerable schistocytes, confirming thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA). Serum LDH: Markedly elevated, declining with therapy. Serology: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, HIV, and antinuclear antibody (ANA) were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain MRI: Normal without evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or intracranial mass lesions.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) / secondary thrombotic microangiopathy triggered by acute co-infection with Dengue and Chikungunya viruses in a patient with underlying ITP. Diagnostic confirmation: Serology positive for Dengue virus IgM (with subsequent IgG seroconversion) and Chikungunya virus IgM and IgG; peripheral smear demonstrating innumerable schistocytes and elevated LDH; exclusion of viral hepatitis, HIV, and SLE.
Plan & Outcome: Managed in ICU with pulse methylprednisolone therapy and daily therapeutic plasma exchange (plasmapheresis). Achieved complete neurological recovery following the initial plasma exchange session. Plasmapheresis was discontinued after platelet counts sustained >150,000/mm3 for three consecutive days, leading to full clinical and hematological recovery.
